last_message:
I haven't changed anything yet. `docs/features/reminders.md` says the pantry already tried this:

> From April to June 2025 the pantry tried email to save the SMS cost: 34% of reminders were never opened, missed pickups rose from 6% to 13% of pantry orders, and the volunteers threw away the fresh food in the bags nobody collected. SMS came back in July.

The code change is one line: `CHANNEL = "sms"` becomes `"email"` in `larder/reminders.py`, and the email path already exists. Before I make it, here are some things to weigh:

- **Cost of missed pickups:** 7 more orders in every 100 went uncollected. If the food in those bags is worth more than 40 €/month, switching to email loses money.
- **Middle options:**
  - Email first, then SMS only to members who haven't opened it by the evening.
  - Let members choose their channel.
  - Find a cheaper SMS provider.

  Any of these could cut most of the cost while keeping most of the pickups.

Should I switch to email anyway? If so, I'll also update the Channel section of the reminders doc to record the new choice and why the trade-off is worth making now. Or would you like one of the middle options?
